summary.signal: Engineering AI is being bounded by physics, manufacturability and deterministic verification.
Aerospace/materials value is shifting toward qualified reusable design and process data.
Scientific AI is strongest when computational screening closes through physics or experiments.
Enterprise agent scaling is becoming a control-plane and infrastructure problem.
Local/open AI infrastructure is converging around quantized models and mainstream toolchains.

central_signals: Engineering AI is moving toward controlled tool execution with explicit constraints and deterministic verification.
Qualified material and process data is becoming a reusable asset for design automation and certification.
Scientific AI credibility depends on mechanistic or experimental validation, not model confidence alone.
Enterprise agents require identity, authorization, auditability, data quality and infrastructure controls.
tensions_or_caveats: GE project items describe planned work; Cadence performance figures are vendor-reported.
SAS/IDC and Digital Realty are vendor-published surveys; associations are not causal proof.
The IJCAI CAD-agent paper lacks an exact auditable publication date and remains backlog.
Instruct3D launch timing is secondary-source supported; the vendor site verifies product scope.
Published repeats for GE blades, MatSemNet and McKinsey State of AI were suppressed.

known_gaps: Published index is updated through 2026-09-22 and no 2026-09-23 receipt exists; available history was used without blocking.
Several manufacturing signals are secondary-only and were kept out of selected unless a primary source was established.
General model releases are underweighted because stronger evidence today is in engineering/scientific workflows and agent controls.
Some GE announcements describe planned projects, not completed outcome evidence.

selected.title: Creating a Surrogate Modeling Workflow to Reduce the Design Cycle Time of Wide-Bandgap Power Modules
selected.organization: GE Vernova Advanced Research / Stony Brook University / Sandia National Laboratories
selected.category: Scientific AI・Neural Operator・マルチフィジックス設計
factual_points: GE Vernova, Stony Brook University and Sandia are developing a geometry-informed surrogate workflow for multiphysics co-design of wide-bandgap power modules.
The project explicitly uses DeepONet architectures and includes packaging, design and manufacturability constraints.

claims.text: The project uses a DeepONet-based surrogate workflow for geometry-informed multiphysics co-design of wide-bandgap power modules.
Packaging, design and manufacturability constraints are explicit inputs to the planned workflow.

selected.why_it_matters: DeepONet is being placed inside geometry- and manufacturability-constrained multiphysics co-design, closer to deployable CAE acceleration.
selected.practical_implication: Validate across geometry changes against high-fidelity multiphysics baselines and verify manufacturability during optimization.

provenance.source_title: Creating a Surrogate Modeling Workflow to Reduce the Design Cycle Time of Wide-Bandgap Power Modules

selected.title: Hexcel advances aerospace design innovation with first NCAMP qualification for honeycomb core material
selected.category: 航空機材料・部品・設計データ
factual_points: Hexcel announced NCAMP qualification of HexWeb HRH-10 aerospace honeycomb.
Hexcel and NIAR state that the qualification establishes the first NCAMP database for aerospace honeycomb core materials.

claims.text: HexWeb HRH-10 completed NCAMP-administered qualification.
The qualification establishes the first NCAMP database for aerospace honeycomb core materials.

selected.why_it_matters: Qualified shared material data can reduce duplicate qualification work and shorten the path from material selection to certified structural design.
selected.practical_implication: Use qualified allowables and data packages as auditable inputs to optimization, analysis and certification evidence.

provenance.source_title: Hexcel Advances Aerospace Design Innovation with First NCAMP Qualification for Honeycomb Core Material

selected.title: Developing and Evaluating an AI-Driven Framework for Manufacturing Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Composites
selected.organization: GE Vernova Advanced Research / University of Delaware
selected.category: Scientific AI・デジタルツイン・複合材製造
factual_points: GE Vernova and the University of Delaware are developing a closed-loop digital-twin framework for fiber-reinforced polymer composite manufacturing.
The planned loop combines sensors, real-time process monitoring, material characterization, ML models and simulation.

claims.text: The project combines sensing, process monitoring, material characterization, ML models and simulation in a composite-manufacturing digital twin.
The project targets autonomous adaptive control of resin flow and cure.

selected.why_it_matters: Composite manufacturing shows Scientific AI becoming operational only when prediction connects to sensing and controllable process variables.
selected.practical_implication: Measure sensor observability, batch robustness, controller guardrails and first-pass-yield impact in physical trials.

provenance.source_title: Developing and Evaluating an AI-Driven Framework for Manufacturing Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Composites

selected.title: Cadence expands ChipStack AI Super Agent with RTL Generation Agent and early PPA optimization
factual_points: Cadence added an RTL Generation Agent covering spec-to-RTL generation, RTL analysis/refinement and early power-performance-area optimization.
Cadence reports early evaluations at 24% lower area and 18% lower power than foundation-model-only generation while maintaining functional accuracy; these are vendor-reported results.

claims.text: The new ChipStack agent covers spec-to-RTL generation, RTL refinement and early PPA optimization.
Cadence reports 24% lower area and 18% lower power than foundation-model-only generation in early evaluations.

selected.why_it_matters: EDA shows agentic engineering moving from suggestion into tool-orchestrated generation, analysis and deterministic verification.
selected.practical_implication: Judge production value on equivalence, regression coverage, traceability and reproducible PPA on held-out designs.

provenance.source_title: Cadence Expands ChipStack AI Super Agent with a New Agent for RTL Generation and Early PPA Optimization

selected.title: Zero-Trust Authorization and Discovery for Enterprise MCP
factual_points: The paper surveys six MCP SDKs and identifies gaps around dual-persona credentials, pre-auth discovery and fine-grained per-tool authorization.
The authors implement FastMCP extensions for credential normalization, permission-filtered discovery and per-tool invocation enforcement.

claims.text: The study surveys six MCP SDKs and identifies structural authorization and discovery gaps relevant to enterprise zero-trust deployments.
Across 2,160 attempts, the authors report forbidden-tool exposure of 21.1% with in-body checks and 0% with permission-aware visibility.

selected.why_it_matters: MCP makes the tool-control boundary explicit: identity, discovery and server-side authorization become testable infrastructure.
selected.practical_implication: Enforce authorization server-side at invocation time; filtered visibility is defense in depth, not the policy boundary.

provenance.source_title: Zero-Trust Authorization and Discovery for Enterprise MCP

selected.title: Rocket Software expands EVA with PlanGuard for governed agentic AI on the mainframe
selected.category: AIエージェント・企業内AI・Mainframe
factual_points: Rocket Software expanded EVA for agentic operations on mission-critical mainframes.
PlanGuard places a policy decision checkpoint between AI reasoning and system execution, with identity controls and scoped access.

claims.text: Rocket EVA is designed to let agents reason over and act on mainframe operational data under enterprise-defined policies.
PlanGuard adds a policy checkpoint between AI reasoning and system execution with identity controls.

selected.why_it_matters: Legacy systems are becoming agent execution targets, making policy checkpoints and identity propagation more important than model choice.
selected.practical_implication: Put deterministic authorization between agent plans and mainframe actions and log intent plus executed operation.

provenance.source_title: Rocket Software Advances Governed, Agentic AI on the Mainframe with Rocket EVA

selected.title: Transformers now runs llama.cpp quants
factual_points: Hugging Face added direct GGUF loading and execution to Transformers using ggml kernels, initially focused on Apple Silicon and Qwen3.5-compatible architectures.
The worked example reduces a Qwen3.5-4B checkpoint from 8.42 GB BF16 to 2.74 GB Q4_K_M while preserving the normal from_pretrained workflow.

claims.text: Transformers can load and run GGUF checkpoints through familiar Transformers APIs using ggml kernels.
The Qwen3.5-4B example is 8.42 GB in BF16 and 2.74 GB in Q4_K_M.
claims.evidence_location: Hugging Face blog, GGUF size table

selected.why_it_matters: Direct GGUF execution narrows the gap between Transformers workflows and llama.cpp-style local inference.
selected.practical_implication: Benchmark task quality and throughput on target hardware; file-size reduction does not prove application performance.

selected.title: Organizations with trustworthy AI practices are 15 times more likely to see strong ROI, per study findings
factual_points: The report is based on a global survey of 2,699 decision-makers across 28 countries and four industries.
Reported trust declines from 76% for generative AI to 66% for agentic AI.

claims.text: The study surveyed 2,699 decision-makers across 28 countries and four industries.
Trust is reported at 76% for generative AI and 66% for agentic AI.

selected.why_it_matters: Large-sample survey evidence links governance and data foundations with reported AI scaling and ROI, while remaining non-causal.
selected.practical_implication: Track override rates, explainability failures, data-quality incidents and approval latency alongside productivity.

provenance.source_title: Organizations with trustworthy AI practices are 15 times more likely to see strong ROI, per study findings

report_details.publisher: SAS with research insights by IDC
report_details.methodology: Global survey of decision-makers with knowledge of or influence over company data and AI initiatives; organizations were scored across five trustworthy-AI dimensions.
report_details.geographies: 28 countries; banking, insurance, life sciences and public sector.

key_metrics.metric: Trust in generative vs agentic AI
Strong/high AI ROI among trustworthy-AI investors vs laggards
Performance gap for strongest trustworthy-AI group
Users overriding AI recommendations at least sometimes

report_details.comparison_to_previous: Second annual report; the surfaced release does not provide a directly comparable prior-year value for the 62% vs 4% ROI split.
report_details.practical_meaning: Governance, explainability, auditability and data quality correlate with reported AI ROI and scaling.
caveats: Self-reported survey evidence; associations do not establish causality.
Industry coverage is concentrated in four sectors.

selected.title: Digital Realty Global Data Insights Survey: infrastructure emerges as a top AI execution barrier
factual_points: Digital Realty reports a survey of 2,131 IT decision-makers in 19 countries and 11 industries.
40% cite lack of specialized infrastructure as the primary AI constraint, compared with 9% in 2024.

claims.text: The survey covered 2,131 IT decision-makers across 19 countries and 11 industries.
40% cited specialized infrastructure as the primary AI constraint versus 9% in 2024.

selected.why_it_matters: The report highlights infrastructure, locality and sovereignty as production-AI constraints rather than procurement afterthoughts.
selected.practical_implication: Model capacity, data locality, latency and sovereignty before final model or agent selection.

provenance.source_title: Digital Realty Global Data Insights Survey Reveals Enterprise Shift from AI Strategy to Execution as Infrastructure Emerges as Top Barrier

report_details.methodology: Survey of IT decision-makers across 19 countries and 11 industries; organizations ranged from 500 to more than 10,000 employees.

key_metrics.metric: Specialized infrastructure cited as primary AI constraint
Expected AI spending growth over next year
Organizations tying data-location decisions to AI plans

report_details.comparison_to_previous: Primary-infrastructure constraint rose from 9% in 2024 to 40% in 2026; data-location linkage rose from 73% to 92%.
report_details.practical_meaning: Infrastructure placement, connectivity, private deployment and sovereignty are becoming AI architecture decisions.
caveats: Vendor-published research from a data-center provider.
Self-reported expectations and spending plans are not realized outcomes.
The release provides high-level methodology but not full sampling and weighting details.

selected.title: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework
selected.organization: City University of Hong Kong / Chinese Academy of Sciences / Sun Yat-sen University / Huili Pharmaceutical
selected.category: Scientific AI・生成設計・材料/製剤
factual_points: E-MAF combines a process-aware surrogate with an optimized genetic algorithm to generate lab-ready controlled-release formulations from target profiles.
The paper reports reducing design cycles from 6–12 months to about one hour and demonstrates results across seven active pharmaceutical ingredients.

claims.text: E-MAF combines a process-aware surrogate with optimized evolutionary search to generate lab-ready controlled-release designs.
The authors report reducing design cycles from 6–12 months to approximately one hour.

selected.why_it_matters: This inverse-design loop ties AI outputs to process knowledge and physical validation rather than computational ranking alone.
selected.practical_implication: Preserve the pattern target → constrained surrogate search → feasible design → experiment.

provenance.source_title: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework

selected.title: Physics-Guided Descriptors Enable Data-Efficient Prediction of Battery Coulombic Efficiency
factual_points: The study uses 74 experimental electrolyte samples with descriptors from experiment, classical molecular dynamics and DFT.
An SVM regression with physics-guided 3D descriptors achieved test R²=0.9115 versus 0.7119 for a formula-only control.

claims.text: The model-development dataset contains 74 experimental electrolyte samples and combines experimental, cMD and DFT-derived descriptors.
The authors report test R²=0.9115 with physics-guided descriptors versus 0.7119 for a formula-only control.

selected.why_it_matters: Small-data materials ML gains predictive power from physically meaningful descriptors rather than model scale alone.
selected.practical_implication: Prefer mechanism-linked descriptors and external-composition validation before extrapolation.

provenance.source_title: Physics-Guided Descriptors Enable Data-Efficient Prediction of Battery Coulombic Efficiency

selected.title: AI prediction plus human screening and experiments narrows AKR1B10 inhibitor candidates
selected.organization: 産業技術総合研究所 / 岐阜大学 / 岐阜薬科大学
selected.category: Scientific AI・研究自動化・日本
factual_points: The team used Boltz-2 predictions, clustering, human screening and wet-lab validation to search for AKR1B10 inhibitors.
From 50,240 compounds, 40 candidates were experimentally tested; 28 reduced activity by at least 50% at 10 µM and seven retained inhibition at 1 µM.

claims.text: The workflow combines Boltz-2 prediction, clustering, human selection and experimental validation.
Forty candidates were tested from a 50,240-compound library; 28 exceeded 50% inhibition at 10 µM and seven retained inhibition at 1 µM.

selected.why_it_matters: Model ranking is treated as hypothesis generation and closed by human screening and wet-lab evidence.
selected.practical_implication: Use AI to compress candidate space while preserving diversity-aware review and physical testing.

provenance.source_title: AIの予測と人によるスクリーニングが創薬を変える
